title: Repository Guidelines
text: R/: R source files; exported functions documented roxygen2. src/: C++ code via Rcpp/RcppArmadillo; compiled check. tests/testthat/: unit tests (testthat 3rd edition). Top-level tests/testthat.R runs suite. inst/: scripts assets (e.g., HPC .sbatch, CLI helpers, Python utilities). man/, NAMESPACE, DESCRIPTION: package metadata generated docs. vignettes/: long-form examples; built knitr/rmarkdown.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Install deps: Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("devtools"))' (runtime deps come DESCRIPTION). Document: Rscript -e 'devtools::document()' (updates man/ NAMESPACE). Test fast: Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'. Full check: Rscript -e 'devtools::check()' R CMD build . && R CMD check ---cran BrainGnomes_*.tar.gz. Site/docs: Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()' (optional).

title: Repository Guidelines
text: R: 2-space indent, tabs; prefer descriptive snake_case names functions/objects. prefix new helper functions period (.), including internal helpers. Give new functions clear headers describing purpose, inputs, outputs. Use roxygen2 top-level R function headers (@noRd internal helpers) ordinary comment headers nested functions. Add inline documentation non-obvious logic, assumptions, state transitions. C++ (src/): follow tidy, minimal-include style; expose via Rcpp attributes; keep headers local. Roxygen2 docs; include @export, @param, @return, examples practical. File names: group feature (e.g., utils_misc.R, extract_rois.R).

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Every vignettes/*.Rmd file must literal YAML date immediately author, formatted date: "DD Mon YYYY" (example, date: "31 Aug 2026"). creating editing vignette, update date change current local date. Treat documentation, code-chunk, metadata edits alike; defer date update later release step. handing vignette changes, inspect every changed vignette confirm literal date current. release pkgdown preparation, also compare clean vignette git log -1 --date=format:'%d %b %Y' --format='%cd' -- vignettes/<file>.Rmd correct missing stale dates. Keep CRAN builds self-contained: put inline R, git commands, GitHub API calls, network lookups vignette date fields code evaluated building/checking vignettes. Git may used maintainer-side check packaging; committed .Rmd must contain resolved literal date.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Framework: testthat (edition 3). Place tests tests/testthat/ test-*.R. Write small, deterministic tests; avoid HPC external /O possible; use temp files. Run locally devtools::test(); full CI parity via devtools::check().

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Distinguish unit tests HPC-backed integration tests. Prefer local testthat tests mocked scheduler/container behavior pure R logic, reserve Slurm-backed runs code paths truly depend singularity/apptainer, scheduler environment, compute-node-filesystems. container-dependent debugging, prefer interactive Slurm allocation via srun --pty ... bash debugging login node. default way reproduce inspect singularity/apptainer behavior incrementally. Inside interactive allocation, run focused tests rather full suite possible, e.g. Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "prefetch-templateflow-integration-srun")' another narrow filter. Mirror production runtime assumptions testing interactively: bind paths, set APPTAINERENV_* / SINGULARITYENV_* variables, use scratch/log directories, disable networking production script . Treat batch scripts inst/hpc_scripts/ source truth container invocation details. reproducing fMRIPrep/MRIQC/AROMA/FSL behavior, copy bind mounts, environment variables, container command shape relevant .sbatch/.pbs script rather inventing simplified command. Use srun --pty first isolate runtime/container issues quickly. Use sbatch afterward bug may depend non-interactive scheduler behavior, submission wrappers, batch-script-logic. Keep HPC-backed integration tests opt-explicit environment guards skip_if() checks regular devtools::test() remains fast safe machines without Slurm container runtimes. Follow pattern tests/testthat/test-prefetch-templateflow-integration-srun.R future Slurm-backed integration tests need real compute node container runtime. typical interactive workflow : srun --pty -N 1 -n 1 --mem=16g --time=01:00:00 bash load required module/runtime run focused Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "...")' command inside allocation.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Commits: imperative mood, concise subject (≤72 chars), meaningful body needed. PR: run devtools::document(), devtools::test(), devtools::check(); update NEWS.md user-facing changes. PRs include: clear description, linked issues, test updates, relevant screenshots/outputs changes CLI results.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: commit data, PHI, large binaries; use .gitignore inst/ example scripts . Python tools use reticulate; set RETICULATE_PYTHON environment needed. HPC scripts live inst/hpc_scripts/; validate resources locally test queue wide use.

title: BrainGnomes pre-release audit
text: BrainGnomes R package configuring, submitting, monitoring, diagnosing containerized functional MRI workflows high-performance computing clusters. intended users neuroimaging researchers, lab maintainers, research-computing staff operating Slurm TORQUE environments. Users ordinarily create load bg_project_cfg configuration setup_project() load_project(), optionally refine edit_project(), submit selected stages using run_project(), inspect progress get_project_status(), get_subject_status(), diagnose_pipeline(). Supported stages include optional Flywheel synchronization, DICOM--BIDS conversion, standalone BIDS validation, MRIQC, fMRIPrep, ICA-AROMA, BOLD postprocessing, atlas-based ROI time-series/connectivity extraction. package also exposes lower-level BIDS, imaging, filtering, motion, scheduler, job-tracking helpers. implementation combines approximately 18,000 lines R, native image-processing routines, installed Python R helpers, cluster job templates, SQLite tracking, 62 test files, 139 help pages, six installed vignettes. repository shows substantial useful engineering: checks pass, vignettes build, package installation succeeds, installed test run records 1,108 passing assertions. However, release ready: R CMD check fails two installed-package test errors. Direct ROI extraction can silently label Pearson results Spearman another requested estimator connectivity methods resolve filename. Scheduled ROI extraction silently ignores configured estimator computes Pearson correlations instead. Several documented extraction workflows either fail outright silently ignore configuration, including multiple input streams, "none" option, configured masks, disabled time-series output. advertised project-status interface report ROI extraction . issues affect release acceptance interpretation scientific outputs. two connectivity defects especially serious execution can appear successful returned persisted analysis results match requested method.

what: Appendix A. Minimal reusable ROI fixture
title: BrainGnomes pre-release audit
text: following fixture recreates two ROI time series Pearson Spearman correlations materially different. can used build regression tests F02, F03, F05, F06, F07, F09. audited revision, unique-path assertion fails. assertion removed, reported Spearman path contains approximately 0.916869 even though correct Spearman value approximately 0.998665.
code: library(BrainGnomes)  root <- tempfile("braingnomes-audit-") dir.create(root) input_dir <- file.path(root, "input") dir.create(input_dir)  bold_file <- file.path(input_dir, "sub-01_task-rest_desc-clean_bold.nii.gz") atlas_file <- file.path(root, "DemoAtlas.nii.gz")  set.seed(2718) dims <- c(4L, 3L, 2L, 30L) x <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = dims[[4]]) bold <- array(0, dim = dims)  for (i in seq_len(dims[[4]])) {   bold[1:2, , , i] <- 100 + x[[i]] + rnorm(12, sd = 0.03)   bold[3:4, , , i] <- 100 + x[[i]]^3 + rnorm(12, sd = 0.03) }  atlas <- array(0L, dim = dims[1:3]) atlas[1:2, , ] <- 1L atlas[3:4, , ] <- 2L  RNifti::writeNifti(RNifti::asNifti(bold), bold_file) RNifti::writeNifti(RNifti::asNifti(atlas), atlas_file)  result <- extract_rois(   bold_file = bold_file,   atlas_files = atlas_file,   out_dir = root,   cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman"),   min_vox_per_roi = 1L )[[1]]  paths <- unlist(result$correlation) stopifnot(length(unique(paths)) == length(paths))  series <- read.delim(result$timeseries, check.names = FALSE) for (method in names(result$correlation)) {   observed <- as.matrix(     read.delim(result$correlation[[method]], check.names = FALSE)   )[1, 2]   expected <- cor(series$roi1, series$roi2, method = method)   stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(observed, expected, tolerance = 1e-7))) }

title: BrainGnomes Quickstart
text: BrainGnomes R package streamlines preprocessing analysis fMRI data high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. serves wrapper around common fMRI processing tools HeuDiConv (DICOM--BIDS conversion), BIDS Validator, MRIQC (quality control), fMRIPrep (preprocessing pipeline), ICA-AROMA (automatic removal motion artifacts), orchestrating execution coherent pipeline. BIDS validation configured project submitted separately run_bids_validation(). package also provides additional processing steps preparing fMRI data analysis, spatial smoothing, temporal filtering, confound regression. BrainGnomes uses containerized software (Singularity images) ensure reproducible environments imaging tools manages job submission HPC schedulers (SLURM TORQUE). tutorial, walk full workflow setting running fMRI preprocessing study using BrainGnomes. cover three key functions: setup_project(): Initialize new study configuration (either scratch existing YAML configuration file) edit_project(): Interactively review modify study configuration sections run_project(): Execute preprocessing pipeline steps dataset, utilizing HPC environment Along way, assume required Singularity container images tool working HPC environment. Additional information setting compute environment provided BrainGnomes Singularity container setup. vignette provides example R code snippets, explains expected inputs outputs, offers troubleshooting tips common issues. end guide, new user understand configure study launch BrainGnomes pipeline start finish. Full pipeline submission designed HPC clusters using SLURM TORQUE/PBS. package can installed loaded standard computer, configuration inspection, BIDS helpers, status-table handling, native imaging helpers remain available. See Local onboarding prerequisites executable -cluster introduction.

code: demo_dir <- tempfile("braingnomes_motion_qc_") dir.create(demo_dir)  make_demo_confounds <- function(subject, spike_size) {   n_volumes <- 120L   volume <- seq_len(n_volumes)   respiration <- sin(2 * pi * volume / 4)   slow_drift <- sin(2 * pi * volume / 48)    motion <- data.frame(     rot_x = 0.0015 * respiration + 0.0005 * slow_drift,     rot_y = 0.0010 * cos(2 * pi * volume / 4),     rot_z = 0.0004 * slow_drift,     trans_x = 0.06 * respiration + 0.02 * slow_drift,     trans_y = 0.03 * cos(2 * pi * volume / 4),     trans_z = 0.01 * slow_drift   )   motion$trans_x[c(45L, 88L)] <-     motion$trans_x[c(45L, 88L)] + c(spike_size, -spike_size)    differences <- rbind(0, diff(as.matrix(motion)))   motion$framewise_displacement <-     rowSums(abs(differences[, 1:3, drop = FALSE])) * 50 +     rowSums(abs(differences[, 4:6, drop = FALSE]))    output <- file.path(     demo_dir,     sprintf(       "sub-%s_ses-01_task-rest_run-01_desc-confounds_timeseries.tsv",       subject     )   )   utils::write.table(     motion,     file = output,     sep = "\t",     quote = FALSE,     row.names = FALSE,     na = "n/a"   )   output }  demo_files <- c(   make_demo_confounds("01", spike_size = 0.35),   make_demo_confounds("02", spike_size = 0.80) ) basename(demo_files) #> [1] "sub-01_ses-01_task-rest_run-01_desc-confounds_timeseries.tsv" #> [2] "sub-02_ses-01_task-rest_run-01_desc-confounds_timeseries.tsv"

text: function mimics AFNI's 3dAutomask logic generate binary brain mask 3D 4D NIfTI image. input 4D, time dimension collapsed computing mean image across frames. robust clip level estimated, voxels threshold retained, morphological clean-steps applied (largest component, peels, hole-filling, optional erosion/dilation, optional superior–inferior cutoff).

code: automask(img, outfile = "", clfrac = 0.5, NN = 2L,   erode_steps = 0L, dilate_steps = 0L, SIhh = 0, peels = 1L,   fill_holes = TRUE)

title: Create an automatic brain mask from a NIfTI image (Rcpp implementation) — automask
text: img RNifti::NiftiImage object containing 3D 4D volume file path NIfTI object whose mask calculated outfile Optional file path resulting mask saved NIfTI file. "" (default), file written. clfrac Fraction median intensity current clip used iterative clip estimator. Smaller values produce larger masks. Default 0.5. NN Neighborhood connectivity used largest connected component search optional morphology. Options 1 (faces , 6-neighbor), 2 (faces+edges, 18-neighbor), 3 (faces+edges+corners, 26-neighbor). Default 2. erode_steps Number additional erosions apply main mask construction. Default 0 (none). dilate_steps Number additional dilations apply main mask construction. Default 0 (none). SIhh Distance millimeters superior voxel mask retain. Voxels inferior cutoff set zero. Default 0 (cutoff). peels Number layer-aware peel/restore operations using NN2 neighborhood AFNI's 17--18 survival rule. remove thin protuberances restoring boundary voxels connected surviving core. Default 1, matching AFNI 3dAutomask. fill_holes Logical; TRUE, interior holes mask filled using NN=1 connectivity. Default TRUE.

title: Create an automatic brain mask from a NIfTI image (Rcpp implementation) — automask
text: 3D RNifti mask object dimensions c(nx, ny, nz) values 0/1. outfile provided, mask also written disk unsigned 8-bit (DT_UINT8) NIfTI file.

title: Create an automatic brain mask from a NIfTI image (Rcpp implementation) — automask
text: processing pipeline follows: Collapse 4D inputs 3D mean volume. Compute iterative global clip threshold, estimate local clip levels eight overlapping regions, apply smoothly interpolated spatial threshold. Retain largest connected component (NN specified). Apply AFNI-style 17--18 layer-aware peeling restoration (peels times, NN2), retain largest face-connected surviving component. Optionally fill interior holes. Apply user-specified erosion/dilation steps (NN specified). Apply optional superior–inferior cutoff (SIhh).

Default: FALSE. atlas_space Optional fallback coordinate-space label atlas files contain formal BIDS space-<label> filename entity, "MNI152NLin2009cAsym". filename entity used present; conflicting fallback error. space declaration required atlas resampling enabled grid mismatch encountered.
